Edit
ED-it
noun (Gen Alpha slang)
From English edit, to revise or prepare for publication (back-formed from editor, eighteenth century). As a Gen Alpha noun, an edit is a short fan-made video montage — clips of an athlete, anime character, movie hero, or "sigma" figure cut to music (often phonk), with slow motion, flashes, and transitions — made in apps like CapCut (2020) and posted to TikTok and YouTube Shorts. "That’s so edit" or "edit-worthy" praises a dramatic moment; "velocity edit" names the speed-ramp style. In Fortnite, "edit" also means reshaping a built wall.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

An edit is a fast, dramatic fan video — a hero’s best moments cut to pounding music, slow-mo, and flashes. Gen Alpha children watch hundreds of them, and many make their own. The Christian observation: an edit is the art of showing only the glory. It cuts away the boring parts, the failures, the ordinary days, and leaves a person looking like a god. That is an old human habit with an old name in Scripture: idolatry — giving a creature the glory that belongs to the Creator. "Little children, keep yourselves from idols" (1Jn 5:21). The edit also trains a child to see her own life as a highlight reel and to be disappointed with the uncut version. But God sees the whole film, and He loves it: "we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal" (2Co 4:18). And the best "edit" in the world is not ours but God’s — "whatsoever things are true... honest... just... pure... lovely... think on these things" (Php 4:8). A father can tell a five-year-old: "Videos only show the cool parts. But God sees all of you — even the boring and the hard parts — and He loves the whole you."

Webster 1828 Definition

Fan-made music montage of a hero’s highlights (CapCut era, 2020-) — the art of showing only the glory, which tilts toward idolizing people and editing one’s own life into a highlight reel.

EDIT, n. (Gen Alpha / Gen-Z usage, c. 2020–present) A short fan-made video montage of clips set to music, often phonk, with dramatic effects. "Did you see the Messi edit?"

Styles: velocity edit, sigma edit, anime edit, phonk edit.

Fortnite sense: to reshape a built wall, floor, or ramp ("fast edits").

Decode for parents: notice who the edits glorify; children imitate the figures they watch edited.

Webster 1828, the root — EDIT, v.t. Properly, to publish; more usually, to superintend a publication; to prepare a book or paper for the public eye, by writing, correcting or selecting the matter.

Key Scripture

1Jn 5:21 — "Little children, keep yourselves from idols. Amen."

2Co 4:18 — "While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal."

Php 4:8 — "Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things."

Psa 115:8 — "They that make them are like unto them; so is every one that trusteth in them."

Modern Corruption

The edit cuts a life down to its glory shots and sets it to a beat; it trains children to idolize the edited and to despise their own uncut lives.

expand to see more

Edits are a powerful form of persuasion. The figures they glorify — often brooding, violent, or vain characters — are given the soundtrack of triumph, and children absorb the message that this is what greatness looks like. "They that make them are like unto them; so is every one that trusteth in them" (Psa 115:8): what we watch exalted, we become.

Teach your child to ask of every edit: who is being glorified, and for what? Then let him make edits of better things — a family trip, a brother’s goal, a grandfather’s stories. The craft is not evil; the worship is. And remind him that God loves his uncut life.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Latin edere (to put forth, publish) → editor → back-formed edit (18th c.) → Gen Alpha edit, a fan montage (c. 2020).
